# Best portable power stations for camping

The right size depends on your trip. Reviewers agree the best pick for most campers is a light 250-500Wh unit, and you only need to go bigger for a fridge, multi-day trips, or several people.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
The 288Wh class (about 8-10 lb) is the sweet spot, per [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/):

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb): their top overall pick. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so check which one you're getting.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC): their best value. It's expandable to 572Wh.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh): has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard C300 with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" variant.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC): the budget option.

Those picks come from an affiliate-supported site. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) scored the Anker C300 (50) and Jackery Explorer 300 (52) fairly low in its lab tests, though it still named the Explorer 300 best for phones and laptops. If you only need to charge devices, any of these will work. If you want more capability, step up a size.

## Multi-day trips, a 12V fridge, or a group
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (39 lb, 2,042Wh, 2,200W): OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It was listed under $900 on Amazon at last check.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh): [TechRadar's](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations) camping pick. PowerStationGearLab calls it their van/overland choice.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (1,536Wh, ~40 lb, IP65 water and dust rating): [WIRED's](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/) best for camping, at $1,079 on sale.

## Best mid-range value
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value, listed under $530 on sale. It's compact, but its fan is noisy.
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, ~35 lb): $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180). It has a 5-year warranty and no expansion port. Dealectric is an affiliate site, and the code's price was last verified 2026-10-21.

## Quick sizing tips
- A phone charge takes about 10Wh, and a CPAP night takes 30-60Wh with the humidifier off.
- A fridge or electric cooler needs a roughly 1kWh unit or larger.
- A folding solar panel is worth adding for trips longer than a weekend.

I couldn't get direct retailer product URLs from these results, so the links above go to the reviews, which have the current price and purchase buttons. Prices change often, and Black Friday is close, so check before you buy.

If you tell me your gear (CPAP, fridge, number of nights) and budget, I can narrow it to one pick.
